claims.claim: Epiphanius was bishop of Salamis on Cyprus from about 367 until 402.
Epiphanius was a witness to and participant in the troubled era after the Council of Nicaea.

Books II and III of the Panarion deal with the Trinity, the Person of Christ, the divinity and personality of the Holy Spirit, Manichaeism, penance, matrimony and celibacy, monastic regulations, and the Christian Calendar.
Epiphanius was present at a synod in Antioch in 376 where Trinitarian questions were debated against the heresy of Apollinarianism.
Epiphanius upheld the position of Bishop Paulinus, who had the support of Rome, over that of Meletius of Antioch, who was supported by the Eastern Churches.
